author: Vieillot, 1816
status: 나그네새, 해마다 수천 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록(10건 미만)
habitat: 간척지, 하구의 삼각주, 논, 염전, 해안 갯바위
summary: 봄과 가을에 흔하게 지나가는 나그네새다. 간척지, 하구의 삼각주, 논, 염전, 해안 갯바위 등지에서 작은 무리를 지어 지내며, 곤충과 갑각류 등 여러 무척추동물을 잡아먹는다. 시베리아 동북부에서 번식하고 동남아시아, 뉴기니, 호주에서 겨울을 난다.

breeding: fine blackish-grey bars on breast and axillaries

art.subject: Grey-tailed Tattler (Tringa brevipes), adult in breeding plumage as seen on Korean coasts in May: crown, hindneck, back, wings and tail uniform plain ash-grey with no spots or streaks; a white supercilium from the bill base to well behind the eye, above a dark grey loral and eye stripe; chin and throat white; breast, neck-sides and flanks finely barred with thin grey to blackish-grey wavy lines; centre of the belly and undertail coverts unbarred white. Bill dark greyish-brown, blackish towards the tip, with a paler yellowish-olive base to the lower mandible; dark eye; legs short and bright yellow.
art.pose: standing on a wet rock at the shoreline, picking at prey
art.scene: Korean coast during spring migration in May: rocky shoreline beside a tidal flat; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding plumage (May), side view standing on a rock: uniform ash-grey upperparts, white supercilium over a dark eye-stripe, fine grey bars on breast, neck-sides and flanks, unbarred white belly centre, short bright yellow legs
adult, head close-up in side view: white supercilium from the bill base to behind the eye, dark loral stripe, straight bill dark brownish-grey with a paler yellowish-olive base
adult non-breeding plumage, side view standing: plain grey upperparts, unbarred pale grey wash across the breast, white belly, white supercilium, yellow legs
art.build: Medium-sized, stocky, horizontal sandpiper, 25cm, about the length of a Common Starling but much bulkier and clearly larger than Common Sandpiper; short neck, often bobbing the rear body. Bill straight, fairly stout, a little longer than the head. Legs short, bright yellow, with little bare tibia. At rest the wingtips reach or slightly pass the tail tip. In flight the upperwing, back, rump and tail are uniform grey with no wing-bar and no white rump; the underwing is dark grey.
avoid: Do not paint a white rump or a white wing-bar; the whole upperside is plain grey.
Do not add spots, streaks or scalloping to the grey upperparts of adults.
Do not bar the belly centre and the undertail; the barring is confined to breast, neck-sides and flanks.
Do not paint long or greenish legs; they are short and bright yellow.
